claims.text: The initial alloy has composition Ti35Ni35Al10Cr10Mo10 in atomic percent.
Ti35Ni35Al10Cr10Mo10 satisfies the stated high-entropy-alloy requirement that every constituent be present at 5–35 at%.
Adding 10 at% Al and aging at 725–775°C for 4–6 hours will form a uniform nanoscale precipitate dispersion.
The precipitates produced by the intervention will be coherent B2-ordered Ti–Ni aluminides.
The coherent B2 precipitates will be embedded in a disordered Ti–Ni matrix.
Coherent B2 precipitates will generate local coherency-strain fields.
The coherency-strain fields will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will retard elevated-temperature dislocation glide and creep.
The intervention will increase high-temperature yield strength by at least 15–20% at 700–800°C relative to the baseline.
The intervention will improve creep-rupture resistance at 700–800°C relative to the baseline.
Homogenization at approximately 1200°C followed by quenching, without the intervention, leaves the baseline alloy as a homogeneous solid solution without beneficial nanoscale precipitation.
Aging at 725–775°C for 4–6 hours constitutes a subsolvus treatment for the proposed alloy.
Confining aging to 725–775°C for 4–6 hours will avoid coarse deleterious phases and maintain precipitate coherence.
The proposed microstructure is intended to support improved mechanical performance at operating temperatures up to 800°C.

contradictions.description: The stated initial composition already sums to 100 at%, but the intervention adds another 10 at% Al without identifying which constituents are reduced or giving a normalized modified composition. Thus the post-intervention composition and its compliance with the 5–35 at% boundary are undefined.

The experiment says both groups have composition Ti35Ni35Al10Cr10Mo10, while also saying the experimental group receives an additional 10 at% Al. The experimental group cannot retain the stated composition after that addition.

The predicted comparison attributes the outcome to both supplemental Al and aging, whereas the baseline and experimental design inconsistently describe the groups as similarly or identically composed. Consequently, it is unclear whether the comparison isolates aging, Al addition, or their combination.
